ht4d5.report_header:
Short statement of results
-   Claim Summary​. The claim selected for replication from Nyhan and Reifler (2015) was
that providing an alternative causal explanation helps prevent new misperceptions from
taking root (e.g., Johnson & Seifert, 1994). This claim was reflected by the statement
from the abstract that, "[We] find that a causal explanation for an unexplained event is
significantly more effective than a denial even when the denial is backed by unusually
strong evidence." The original claim was tested by regressing respondents' beliefs that a
fictional politician is resigning from office because he is under investigation for bribery on
an indicator variable for the respondent being randomly assigned to read an article
where the politician's resignation is suggested to be because of a bribery investigation
along with a denial from the politician (denial condition) and an indicator variable for the
respondent being assigned to an article that is the same as the article in the denial
condition but with additional information that provides an alternative causal explanation
for the resignation (causal correction condition), with the excluded category being the
respondent only read the suggestion about bribery without a denial or alternative causal
explanation (innuendo condition) -- using inverse probability weights. The results of the
test were a coefficient on the denial indicator of -0.25 (SE = 0.07) and a coefficient on

I. Claim summary:
This reproduction tests the claim from Smith et al. (2016) that classrooms with a larger share of natives show less ethnic homophily.
The selected claim is tested using a two-step procedure. In a first step, the authors estimate ethnic homophily in classes using exponential random graph models (ERGMs) for each school class separately. In a second step, the authors examine the combined effects using a metaregression.
The exact model we are asked to replicate comes from Table 3, Model 2. The dependent variable is the (estimated) level of ethnic homophily in the classroom.  The focal estimate in Table 3, Model 2 concerns the coefficient on the “Proportion natives” variable. The coefficient is negatively signed and statistically significant (b = -.51, SE = .06, p < .001), and thus  provides evidence in support of the hypothesis that ethnic homophily decreases with an increasing share of natives.
II. Reproduction criteria:
A successful replication of the Smith et al. (2016) results would be a statistically significant negative effect (alpha = .05, two tailed) of the share of natives on ethnic homophily in the meta-analysis regression model.
III. Reproduction result:
Our replication of Model 2 in Table 3  yields a coefficient of  b = -.47 (SE = .07, p < .001) on  the “Proportion natives” variable (see Table 1 in the attached Appendix).  Thus, this reproduction of the claim was successful according to the SCORE criteria.

8uc5z.report_header:
Short statement of results
-   Claim Summary​. The claim selected for replication from Nyhan and Reifler (2015) was
that providing an alternative causal explanation helps prevent new misperceptions from
taking root (e.g., Johnson & Seifert, 1994). This claim was reflected by the statement
from the abstract that, "[We] find that a causal explanation for an unexplained event is
significantly more effective than a denial even when the denial is backed by unusually
strong evidence." The original claim was tested by regressing respondents' beliefs that a
fictional politician is resigning from office because he is under investigation for bribery on
an indicator variable for the respondent being randomly assigned to read an article
where the politician's resignation is suggested to be because of a bribery investigation
along with a denial from the politician (denial condition) and an indicator variable for the
respondent being assigned to an article that is the same as the article in the denial
condition but with additional information that provides an alternative causal explanation
for the resignation (causal correction condition), with the excluded category being the
respondent only read the suggestion about bribery without a denial or alternative causal
explanation (innuendo condition) -- using inverse probability weights. The results of the
test were a coefficient on the denial indicator of -0.25 (SE = 0.07) and a coefficient on
the causal correction indicator of -0.58 (SE = 0.07). The difference in coefficients was
-0.34 with a p-value less than 0.01.
-   Replication Criteria​. Criteria for a successful replication is a statistically significant
effect (alpha = .05) in the same direction as the original finding -- namely, the casual
correction effect being stronger than the denial effect.
